expected_behavior: A round that ships lifecycle or state-machine code alongside canonical prose gets both instrument classes before its executed-verdict gate: one static pass for doc/registry truth, one executing adversarial pass for semantics — neither substitutes for the other.
observation: Two review instruments with different postures — the fleet's read-only prose/threat lanes and an executing adversarial reviewer — produced nearly disjoint finding sets across two full cycles of the same branch: the static lanes caught documentation-truth, ownership-registry, and contract-drift defects no execution would surface, while the executing reviewer caught lifecycle-semantics defects (views that lose records, unrecordable state cycles) that six prior static rounds of a comparable change class never found.
reason: Rejected 2026-08-20: operator cost ruling never made; encoding a standing two-instrument mandate would add session load this pass is reducing. Evidence retained in this record.
